headline: High: transformers can read/write and browse by default, while the paired awesome-list is non-runnable and provides no isolation, creating default risks of prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable docs-only repo with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. Profile B can read files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout, so if A’s content is manually copied or placed in a shared workspace, B may treat it as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default from A alone.
conditions: IF A’s content is copied into a file or prompt that B ingests
IF B parses external text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate folders
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into B prompts
Add a provenance header to any A-derived text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B has broad network egress plus filesystem read/write and browser access. If sensitive files are placed in B’s workspace, B can transmit them to third parties by default. A is not a leakage source, but its lack of runtime isolation means it does not reduce B’s exposure.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in B’s readable workspace
IF B is allowed to browse or call external APIs with those files
mitigations: Remove sensitive files from B’s workspace
Run B with network disabled for sensitive jobs
Use a separate non-sensitive working directory
Inspect outbound requests before enabling egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but without any writable surface in A there is no meaningful pairwise write conflict. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually maps both to the same directory, which is unusual.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same writable directory
IF B is run concurrently with another writer on the same files
mitigations: Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Run B serially for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an informational repo and B is a document-processing model that can consume text, so A-derived content can become B input. If B then acts on or renders that content without verification, errors can cascade. Because A has no runtime authority, the risk is inference-based rather than directly observed, but B’s pipeline API makes the pathway plausible.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived text as authoritative input
IF B forwards outputs to downstream actions without verification
mitigations: Require human review of B outputs
Add a verification step before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is documented for A, and B’s profile lists no secrets handled or regulated residency constraints. With only docs-only evidence and no PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch shown, a compliance breach pathway is not established. The pairwise interaction is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into B’s workflow
IF residency or retention requirements are later imposed
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
